markdown_report:
At 0% progress, the strongest next step remains a **paired temporal-sensitivity audit for the existing HSTU**, with stronger controls and narrower interpretation.

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Training margins measure sampled-pair separation, not validation ranking quality; memorization and score scale can affect them. (2) Left padding requires the final nonpadding index, never count−1. (3) Feedback distinguishes recent interests from broad associations, but histories cannot establish fulfilled needs or compatibility.

**Related-work insights.** (1) HSTU can use relative-position and bucketed-time biases [1,5]; the supplied implementation’s actual paths must be checked before interpreting perturbations. Deletion and repacking can change both information and coordinates. (2) Controlled shuffling motivates separating final-event dependence from prefix ordering [2], but degradation demonstrates sensitivity under altered inputs, not beneficial temporal reasoning. (3) TREC distinguishes complementarity from unknown compatibility [3]. Missing specifications remain unknown. (4) Sampled metrics can reverse comparisons [4]; repeated adaptive selection also risks validation overfitting [6].

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Existing evidence | Missing measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal dependence | Training margins | Paired information-loss versus coordinate effects |
| Evidence sufficiency | Titles/descriptions | Supported, conflicting, or unknown attributes |
| Ranking robustness | Pinned validation HR@10 | Candidate-dependent disagreement |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means more work.

1. **Paired temporal audit [1,2,5]: 4/6/5.** Originality: + family-specific controls; − established perturbations. Potential: + generates actionable hypotheses; − no established diagnostic-to-improvement relationship. Difficulty: + existing inference hooks; − coordinate controls may require backbone instrumentation.
2. **Evidence-status audit [3]: 5/7/6.** Originality: + separates unknown from conflict; − established attribute auditing. Potential: + exposes unsupported claims; − sparse descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: + inspectable spans; − extraction needs annotated validation.
3. **Candidate stress audit [4]: 3/6/5.** Originality: + connects failures to candidate composition; − established sampling analysis. Potential: + reveals fragility; − cannot replace benchmark selection. Difficulty: + reuses scoring; − eligibility and false negatives require care.

**Selected algorithm.** Cache up to ten loader batches; retain original final-position targets. Run identity controls, equal-count oldest/recent/random deletions preserving the final event, separate final-versus-penultimate deletion, and repeated prefix permutations preserving the final item. Left-pad outputs and extract their final nonpadding features. Report paired margins, ordering flips, feature cosines, eligibility, and missingness.

Audit masks, normalization, positional embeddings and timestamp anchors first [5]. Where supported, compare identical retained subsets with preserved coordinates versus compaction; fully mask deleted keys and queries. Internal holes remain distribution shifts. Item-only shuffles retain chronological timestamp slots; joint item–timestamp shuffles are optional stress tests.

Use available fixed validation candidates for paired ranks and HR@10 only through authorized host evaluation; loader diagnostics cannot supply these. Aggregate repeated observations by user before bootstrap intervals; without identities, report descriptive summaries only. Preserve both entry points and model mode. Keep one checkpoint/category, fixed seeds and limits, routing, predictor consistency and macro validation selection. Predeclare a small ablation sequence; sensitivity supplies no uplift forecast.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152; [2] https://publications.hse.ru/en/chapters/984043670; [3] https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html; [4] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [5] https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/hstu.py; [6] https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/2015/hash/bad5f33780c42f2588878a9d07405083-Abstract.html

idea.description: Strengthen the paired temporal-sensitivity diagnostic for the supplied HSTU ModelView adapter with identity controls, final-event-preserving interventions, explicit coordinate-confounding checks, and dependence-aware reporting. Hold each original positive/negative pair fixed across interventions and interpret results as sensitivity measurements rather than evidence of user intent or expected accuracy gains.
idea.motivation: Existing embedding and margin diagnostics cannot distinguish recent-event dependence, broader ordering effects, or artifacts caused by repacking histories. Qualitative feedback motivates investigating these distinctions, but no supplied evidence establishes that increasing or decreasing perturbation sensitivity improves validation HR@10. This audit should generate hypotheses for subsequent controlled single-model HSTU ablations, without assuming ownership, satisfied needs, compatibility, or unobserved simulator traits.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve view.model as the trained module and the item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data contracts. Use evaluation mode and no_grad, restoring the original mode in finally. Cache at most ten batches; record batch, row, valid-position and eligibility counts. Use local seed-42 randomness and five deterministic permutation/deletion replicates, reporting their count. Do not imply that loader rows are unique users.

Before attributing effects, document the supplied backbone's actual timestamp inputs, relative and absolute position representations, attention masks, aggregation scaling, and normalization. The HSTU reference implementation uses next-position timestamp anchors with endpoint handling, but this does not establish the supplied baseline's behavior. The sequence-only compatibility interface does not establish access to timestamps or arbitrary coordinate masks. If these are unavailable, mark coordinate-controlled and time-specific probes unavailable and describe ordinary deletion as a combined information-and-repacking intervention. Never fabricate timestamps or infer that a sequence-only perturbation isolates time.

Locate each original final nonpadding position with masked position indices. Exclude empty sequences or zero positive/negative targets and report reasons. Freeze that position's original target pair across all interventions. Score original and perturbed final representations using features B x 1 x D and candidates B x 1 x 2 where required by the adapter. For histories of length n >= 3, delete k = max(1, floor(0.2*(n-1))) events from the prefix: its oldest k, most recent k, or k uniformly sampled positions. Preserve the final event in all three conditions. Separately compare removal of the final and penultimate events for n >= 2. These contrasts have different interpretations and must remain separately labeled. Repack retained events with left padding, holding input tensor length fixed. Always extract the altered sequence's actual final nonpadding feature.

For order probes, preserve length, padding, final item and item multiset. Include full-prefix shuffling, adjacent-pair swaps within the prefix, and shuffling before a preserved suffix of min(3, n-1) events; mark cases with fewer than two permutable events ineligible. Preserve chronological timestamp slots for item-only permutations if timestamps exist. Joint item–timestamp permutations are optional, separately labeled nonchronological stress tests. Identity perturbations must reproduce original scores within declared numerical tolerances, for example atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4, with deviations reported.

When backbone instrumentation permits, evaluate identical retained-event subsets under preserved original coordinates and ordinary compaction. Preserve original temporal query anchors explicitly; retaining timestamps alone is insufficient. Fully exclude deleted slots as attention keys and queries and from normalization, while holding tensor length, scaling, candidate pairs and readout conventions fixed. Gathering original relative/time-bias submatrices for compacted sequences is an optional additional control, but absolute embeddings and other coordinate-dependent paths must also be handled. Internal holes can introduce distribution shift, so these contrasts still do not establish causal preference effects. Instrumented identity inference must match ordinary inference before using the control.

Retain embedding geometry diagnostics and training-pair separation metrics. Return raw margins, positive-minus-negative margin changes, negative-wins rates, pairwise-order flips, and feature cosine similarities with explicit denominators. Define small margins as below 0.5 while warning that the threshold is scale-dependent. Use null plus a reason for unavailable measurements, empty samples, or undefined cosine similarities. Item-category breakdowns are unavailable because task metadata excludes those attributes. Use only public histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions; do not access ratings, review text, prices, stores or item categories.

Loader diagnostics cannot calculate validation HR@10. If the authorized host supplies paired fixed-candidate evaluation, retain its users, targets, 99 unique negatives, eligibility rules and seed across interventions; report per-category and macro HR@10 changes, target-rank changes and top-10 overlap. Do not replace the host evaluator or its unperturbed model-selection score. Aggregate repeated histories and intervention replicates within each user before uncertainty estimation; with verified identities, bootstrap users within categories using 1,000 seed-42 resamples and report percentile 95% intervals. Without identities, provide descriptive summaries and explicitly omit user-level intervals. These intervals are conditional on the fitted model and fixed candidates, not training-seed uncertainty.

The interpretation prompt must embed actual measurements, definitions, counts and missingness, distinguish input sensitivity from preference or improvement claims, and avoid numerical uplift forecasts. Predeclare a small subsequent ablation sequence rather than repeatedly mining diagnostics and validation feedback. Select any training change solely by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. The diagnostic proposal requires no retraining or predictor change; any later architecture change must update checkpoint serialization and the embedded predictor writer together. Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, all four routes, single-GPU execution and the shared search budget. Each category must load exactly one independently trained HSTU checkpoint, without independently fitted score fusion or checkpoint averaging.
idea.pseudocode:
audit = document_actual_hstu_paths_and_supported_controls(view)
was_training = view.model.training
view.model.eval()
try:
  with no_grad():
    for batch_id, (_, seq, pos, neg) in enumerate(first_ten_cached_batches):
      end = last_nonpadding_index_using_masked_positions(seq)
      eligible = nonempty_sequence_and_nonzero_targets(seq, pos, neg, end)
      candidates = original_targets_at_end(pos, neg, end)
      original_features = final_nonpadding_feature(view.log2feats(seq), seq)
      original_scores = score_via_modelview(original_features, candidates)
      record_identity_check(seq, original_scores, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)
      plans = deterministic_intervention_plans(seq, seed=42, replicates=5)
      # Prefix deletions share k and preserve the final event.
      # Final and penultimate deletions are separate matched conditions.
      # Prefix permutations preserve declared suffixes and the item multiset.
      for plan in plans:
        altered, intervention_eligible = apply_and_left_pad(seq, plan)
        features = final_nonpadding_feature(view.log2feats(altered), altered)
        scores = score_via_modelview(features, candidates)
        record_paired_metrics(original_scores, scores,
                              original_features, features,
                              eligible & intervention_eligible,
                              batch_id, plan)
        if plan.is_deletion and audit.supports_coordinate_control:
          controlled_scores = score_same_retained_subset_with_original_coordinates(
              view, seq, plan, candidates,
              preserve_query_time_anchors=True,
              exclude_deleted_keys_queries_and_normalization=True)
          record_coordinate_contrast(scores, controlled_scores, plan)
        elif plan.is_deletion:
          record_unavailable_coordinate_control(audit.reason)
    metrics = summarize_counts_missingness_and_paired_effects()
    # Aggregate by verified user IDs before bootstrap; otherwise descriptive only.
    attach_user_intervals_only_if_identity_mapping_is_verified(metrics)
    return {'metrics': metrics,
            'metric_definitions': definitions_with_scope_and_confounding_limits()}
finally:
  view.model.train(was_training)

# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) includes measured values,
# definitions, eligibility and missingness; it requests hypothesis generation
# without causal, compatibility, or expected-validation-uplift claims.
# Paired validation ranks/HR@10 require authorized host evaluation separately.

originality.positive: Adapts established perturbation methods to HSTU's coordinate and temporal-anchor mechanisms while retaining the host diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: The contribution is methodological integration; deletion, permutation and paired sensitivity analysis are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish several sources of observed input sensitivity and support more disciplined choices of subsequent single-model ablations.
future_potential.negative: No supplied study validates sensitivity as a predictor of training improvements, and corrupted-input effects may reflect distribution shift or memorization.

code_difficulty.positive: Basic probes reuse inference hooks and require no additional trained model or external data.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful coordinate and timestamp-anchor controls may require backbone instrumentation; user-level uncertainty and host validation integration need interfaces absent from the loader.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU for recommendation streams and motivates preserving the supplied backbone family.
Describes positional and temporal attention mechanisms relevant to interpreting history perturbations.
limitations: Published results do not establish the supplied checkpoint's temporal sensitivity.
Training-time subsequence selection does not establish robustness to arbitrary inference-time deletion or shuffling.

related_work.title: Meta generative-recommenders: HSTU reference implementation
contributions: Provides implementation evidence for relative-position and bucketed-time biases, including next-position temporal anchors and endpoint handling.
Motivates auditing coordinate, masking and normalization paths before interpreting deletion effects.
limitations: The supplied corrected baseline may implement different paths; its behavior must be inspected directly.
The reference implementation alone does not provide a validated perturbation-control procedure.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Provides precedent for controlled shuffling to examine sequential structure.
limitations: Shuffling can induce distribution shift; observed effects do not identify causal preferences.
The findings do not establish that greater ordering sensitivity improves this HSTU benchmark.

related_work.title: TREC 2025 Recommendation Task
contributions: Distinguishes complementary relevance from established compatibility, including unknown compatibility.
limitations: Its framework supplies no compatibility labels for these Amazon histories.
Substitution and purchase histories do not establish redundant ownership or fulfilled needs.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can change model comparisons.
limitations: Does not calibrate this benchmark's sampled HR@10 to full-catalog performance.
Fixed candidates support paired benchmark comparisons but do not establish population-wide relevance.

related_work.title: The Reusable Holdout: Preserving Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
contributions: Explains how repeated adaptive use of evaluation feedback can compromise generalization claims.
Motivates limiting and predeclaring diagnostic-driven model ablations.
limitations: Does not quantify the overfitting risk of this particular search.
The proposed audit does not implement its reusable-holdout mechanism or obtain additional evaluation data.

related_work.title: Petrov et al. (2026), recency-weighted pairwise recommendation study
contributions: Reports competitive recency-weighted pairwise approaches on several benchmarks, motivating separate examination of recency and higher-order ordering.
limitations: Does not validate perturbation sensitivity as a predictor of HSTU improvements on these four categories.
Provides context for diagnosis rather than authorization to replace HSTU or combine independently fitted scores.
